newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine strike barely affects flights.
newsitem.headline: Argentine strike barely affects flights.

text.p: A general strike called Thursday by opposition unions was having little effect on most Argentine domestic and international airline flights, airline, airport and travel industry officials said.
Argentina's main international airport at Ezeiza near Buenos Aires and Buenos Aires' Jorge Newberry domestic airport were both operating normally, officials said.

A spokesman for flag carrier Aerolineas Argentinas and associated domestic airline Austral said they had reduced the number of domestic flights by 25 percent in anticipation of problems, but all flights were leaving on time.
"As a precaution we altered our schedule and sold our tickets to passengers according to that schedule," spokesman Alejandro Lottito told Reuters, "But that schedule is being met without problems."
Travel agents reported that foreign airlines were operating completely normally, and an official with AMR Corp's American Airlines said his firm had made no changes to the day's schedule.

The CTA and MTA opposition unions called a general strike to protest against unemployment and proposed government labor market reforms. Argentine airline industry unions Wednesday threw their weight behind the strike, saying they hoped to ground all flights.

The pro-government CGT, the country's largest union federation, has reached a deal with the government on labor market reforms and opposes the strike. But its political arm, the "62 Peronist Organizations," supports the stoppage.
This will be the fourth general strike in just over a year against President Carlos Menem's Peronist government. The previous strikes were organized by the CGT.
